title: Flush the sample tap to waste before filling the sample bottle
instruction: Take a water sample: open the tap and let it run to the waste cup for at least ten seconds, then hold the bottle under the tap and fill it to between the two lines, set the bottle on the mark, and close the tap.
context: Harm: a sample taken without flushing the line carries stagnant water and gives a false result; a tap left running floods the bench. Safe finish: tap flushed to waste, bottle filled between the lines, bottle set down upright, tap closed. Rule: Standard Methods 1060 B (flush sample lines before collecting) and the EPA sampling guidance operators follow. Done by: water and wastewater treatment plant operators.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Sample tap, taped down (3 kg): a steel standpipe 3 x 3 cm, 20 cm tall, on a dark floor flange 8 x 5 x 1 cm at x 30, y 0. A steel spout 3 x 3 cm in section runs along the top of the pipe 8.5 cm to the left; its underside is 17 cm up and the stream falls from its tip at x 30, y 7. Lever: a dark plastic bar 8 x 2 x 4 cm sticking out from the pipe's front face towards the arms, centred 9 cm up, sliding 3 cm sideways with 1 cm marks: at its rest (y 0) the tap is shut; pushed 3 cm to the right (y -3) it runs. Waste cup: a grey square collar 7 cm inside, 3 mm walls, 4 cm tall, taped down under the spout's tip at x 30, y 7, draining to a bucket under the bench. Flow lamp: a 2 x 2 x 3 cm lamp at the tap's foot, x 30, y -5, grey when the tap is shut and green while it runs. Bottle: a clear square plastic bottle 5 x 5 cm, 9 cm tall, 3 mm walls, open top, with two blue lines round it 5 and 7 cm up (the 150 and 200 mL marks), in a dark plastic holder: a bar from the bottle's left face at mid-height to a handle post 3 x 2 x 6 cm whose centre is 7 cm left of the bottle's centre and whose top is level with the bottle's top; bottle and holder 80 g, standing at x 20, y 16. Mark: a white plate 7 x 7 cm, 3 mm thick, taped down at x 18, y 26.
scoring: Scored at the end from the water ledger and the end state. The tap runs at 15 mL/s while its lever is pushed at least 70% of its travel (2.1 cm) and is shut when the lever is back within 30% (0.9 cm). Water lands in the bottle when the bottle's mouth is within 2 cm, seen from above, of the point under the spout's tip, below that point and above the cup's rim, and the bottle leans under 30 degrees; otherwise it runs into the waste cup, or onto the bench if the tap has been moved so its spout is off the cup or leans more than 20 degrees. A bottle holding water that leans past 30 degrees empties onto the bench; past 220 mL it overflows. Flushed: at least 150 mL (10 s) ran to waste before the first drop entered the bottle. Filled: 150 to 200 mL in the bottle at the end, between the lines. On the mark: the bottle's centre within 3 cm of the mark's centre, its bottom under 2 cm up, leaning under 15 degrees, with no gripper holding its post. Flushed, filled, on the mark, tap shut: 1.0. Flushed and filled, but the tap open or the bottle not set on the mark: 0.7. Flushed and tap shut, with the bottle under 150 mL or over 200 mL (overfilling earns no fill credit): 0.3. Filled, on the mark and tap shut without the flush: 0.2. Anything else, including nothing done, 0. More than 30 mL on the bench caps the score at 0.5. On a real bench: time the flush on the video, read the level against the lines, measure the bottle's centre to the mark's, and check the lever against its marks.
reset_notes: Slide the lever back to its shut stop and check the lamp is off. Empty the bottle, dry it and stand it in its holder at x 20, y 16. Empty the waste bucket if it is near full. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate. No liquid: a ledger sends 15 mL/s to the cup, the bottle or the bench from the lever's position and the mouth's place under the spout. Nothing is rendered, so the bottle's level is not visible, and the flow lamp stands in for the visible stream. The lever is a slider that moves 3 cm sideways rather than a quarter-turn handle. The bottle's lines mark the ledger's 150 and 200 mL, not its geometric volume. The waste cup drains and never overflows. The bottle is held by a handle post because a straight-down gripper cannot put its mouth under the spout. Rubber-like friction.
